correctness.rationale: For fixed α,ρ∈(0,1), δ>0, conditional on common W=w the e-values are iid lognormal and q_w(t)=P(E≥1/(αt)|W=w). e-BH rejects iff some sorted E_[k]≥K/(αk); for k/K bounded away from zero the empirical tails converge uniformly, and for small k the conditional lognormal tail decays super-polynomially, permitting a binomial/Chernoff geometric control. Thus except at the boundary the rejection event converges to 1{sup_t q_w(t)/t>1}; null FDR equals P(R>0). Equality q_w(t)=t with t=Φbar(x) gives w=g(x)=[log(1/(αΦbar(x)))+δ²/2−s x]/(δ√ρ), s=δ√(1−ρ). The strictly increasing Gaussian hazard h=φ/Φbar has unique h(x*)=s, minimizing g and giving t*=Φbar(x*), w*=g(x*), asymptotic FDR Φbar(w*) by dominated convergence (W continuous). I independently numerically solved h=s: x*=1.71265196548, t*=0.04338829351108, w*=3.29993272728449, FDR=0.000483540037138 at α=.05,δ=3,ρ=.5. The scalar numeric script cannot itself establish the asymptotic small-k step.
residual_risks: The small-order-statistic exclusion requires the conditional lognormal Chernoff argument; the package sketches rather than quantifies a finite-K rate.

value.rationale: A closed-form exact global-null error limit for a canonical dependence model of e-BH answers a substantive question left by general upper bounds, identifies rare common-factor false-rejection bursts and a nonobvious α-independent critical rejection fraction. residual_risks: The formula is only for fixed positive equicorrelation and complete null; no finite-K rate.
